### Tutorial 6.3: Building a Revenue PivotTable from Charles River Data

**Context and objective.** You will build a PivotTable that summarizes Charles River revenue by item group and fiscal quarter. This produces the same output as the SUMIFS table in Tutorial 6.2, but with far less effort and far more flexibility.

**Prerequisites.** Your workbook should contain the merged InvoiceLines dataset, including columns for ItemGroup, FiscalQuarter (or InvoiceDate), and LineTotal.

**Step 1.** Click any cell within your merged data table. Go to the Insert tab and click PivotTable. In the dialog box, confirm that Excel has selected the InvoiceLines table. Select New Worksheet and click OK.

**Step 2.** In the PivotTable Fields pane, drag the ItemGroup field to the Rows area. Excel immediately creates a list of the four item groups as row labels in the PivotTable.

**Step 3.** Drag the LineTotal field to the Values area. Excel creates a column showing "Sum of LineTotal" with the total revenue for each item group. The PivotTable has already produced a one-dimensional revenue summary with a single drag-and-drop action.

**Step 4.** Now add the time dimension. If you have a FiscalQuarter column, drag it to the Columns area. The PivotTable now displays a grid with item groups as rows, quarters as columns, and revenue values in the cells. This is the same structure you built manually in Tutorial 6.2, but Excel generated it automatically.

**Step 5.** If your data contains only the InvoiceDate column without a separate FiscalQuarter field, drag InvoiceDate to the Columns area instead. Excel may group the dates by month automatically. To change the grouping to quarters, right-click any date label in the PivotTable, select Group, and in the Grouping dialog, select Quarters (and optionally Years if your data spans multiple years). Click OK. Excel will regroup the dates into Q1 through Q4.

**Step 6.** Format the PivotTable values as currency. Right-click any revenue value in the PivotTable, select Number Format, choose Currency with zero decimal places, and click OK. The formatting applies to all values in the PivotTable, not just the cell you right-clicked.

**Step 7.** Rename the PivotTable worksheet to "RevenuePivot." Right-click the worksheet tab and select Rename.

**Checkpoint.** Your PivotTable should display four item groups as rows, four fiscal quarters as columns, and formatted revenue values in the cells. Grand totals should appear automatically in the bottom row and the rightmost column. The grand total of approximately $3,332,300 should match the total from your SUMIFS table in Tutorial 6.2 and the total of the LineTotal column in your source data. If the totals do not match, verify that the PivotTable source includes all rows and that no filters are active.

*[Figure 6.4: The completed revenue PivotTable showing item groups as rows, fiscal quarters as columns, currency-formatted revenue values, and grand totals. The PivotTable Fields pane is visible on the right, showing ItemGroup in Rows, FiscalQuarter in Columns, and Sum of LineTotal in Values.]*
